corpusSummary: The 2026 social-science literature on large language models spans methodological innovations, human–AI interaction, education and health applications, and governance. It emphasizes validating AI as a research tool, examining trust and embodiment, exploring AI-assisted learning and counseling, and scrutinizing representation, misinformation, equity, and policy implications. The corpus highlights opportunities and cautions for responsible, evidence-based deployment.

themes.name: AI as a research instrument and methodological frontier
themes.description: Papers frame LLMs as methodological tools for coding, framing analysis, data extraction, simulations, and policy analysis, while demanding validation, transparency, and ethical safeguards.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, embodiment, and social dynamics
themes.description: Studies probe perceived humanness and empathy, AI device embodiment, trust dynamics, and social influence across education, health, and everyday decision-making.

themes.name: AI in education and AI literacy
themes.description: Research maps AI's roles in learning, tutoring, assessment, and literacy, noting benefits for engagement and personalization but risks around overreliance, integrity, and equity.

themes.name: Health, governance, and misinformation in AI deployment
themes.description: A cluster examining AI in health communication, patient education, and governance, including equity-focused audits, misinformation sharing, and safety/quality standards.

emergingKeywords: Equity and ethics in AI deployment
